about.title: McFarland Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: McFarland is a small, tight-knit Kern County community, but that doesn't mean falls don't happen at its markets, gas stations along SR-99, apartment walkways, or agricultural-adjacent businesses near Elmo Highway. Wet floors, uneven pavement, poor lighting in parking areas, and neglected sidewalks can all lead to serious injury in an instant. California law doesn't make these claims automatic — you generally have to show the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why acting quickly matters: photos of the spill or broken step, witness names, and store surveillance footage can disappear fast if nobody asks for them. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened, help gather that evidence, and walk you through your options. There's no cost to talk, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Connect With an Attorney Through LawProactive

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help identify prior complaints, maintenance logs, or repeat incidents that support this.

items.title: Video and Evidence Disappear Quickly
items.desc: Many McFarland businesses recycle surveillance footage within days or weeks. An attorney can send a preservation request fast so that evidence isn't erased before it's reviewed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're told you were partly careless, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a share of damages. An attorney can push back on unfair fault arguments early.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in McFarland?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government-owned property in Kern County is involved, the deadline is much shorter, often just six months to submit a claim. It's best to get an evaluation early so none of these windows close on you.

items.question: What if I fell at a business along SR-99 or Elmo Highway and there's no camera pointed at the spot?
items.answer: Not every location has perfect surveillance coverage, but that doesn't end your claim. An attorney can still rely on photos you took, witness statements, incident reports, and the property's maintenance history to establish what happened and whether the owner had notice of the hazard.

items.question: Does it matter that McFarland is a small town — will an attorney even take a case here?
items.answer: City size doesn't determine whether a premises liability claim has merit; the facts of the fall and the evidence available do. LawProactive connects people throughout Kern County, including McFarland, with independent attorneys who evaluate cases based on those facts, not the population count.
